name: Addons
description: Other mods that add optional content when installed with Aetherhaven
text: Addons Aetherhaven works on its own. Some Hexvane (and partner) mods can optionally plug in when both are installed: extra villagers, shops, quest board jobs, gift tastes, and journal pages. Nothing here is required to run Aetherhaven. Install an addon only if you want that pack’s town content. Known integrations Mod What you get with Aetherhaven ----- ------------------------------- Mechanic villager Rivet Cogsworth , mechanics shop, rescue quest, shop stock Fisherman Reed Castwell , fishing shop, gear/fish shop spots, treasure extras Each overview page explains how to unlock that content. Villager detail pages cover quests, friendship, schedules, and gifts—same style as the Town Journal. For modders Want your mod to appear here? See under For developers.

name: Cozy Tales Fishing
description: Optional Aetherhaven integration from Cozy Tales Fishing
text: Cozy Tales: Fishing Cozy Tales: Fishing is a relaxed fishing pack (rods, bobbers, aquariums, fishing journal). It works alone. With Aetherhaven installed alongside it, you get extra town content. What you get with both mods - Reed Castwell , a castaway fisherman with dialogue and tips - A fishing shop you help establish (blueprint → plot crafting bench → shop prefab) - Shop stock and prices for fishing gear - Extra rewards from sunken treasure (gold coins and the occasional jewelry) Aetherhaven is not required for fishing. Install both only if you want the integration. How to unlock Reed 1. Install Cozy Tales: Fishing and Aetherhaven . 2. Finish Vex's market stall so Reed can appear in the inn visitor pool. 3. Talk to Reed at the inn, accept the fishing shop quest, learn the blueprint at the plot crafting bench, and build the shop. 4. Optionally build Reed a house the same way as other residents. Full quest steps, schedule, and gift tastes: . Related Aetherhaven systems - - - (treasure can drop unidentified pieces)

name: Machinaria
description: Optional Aetherhaven integration from the Machinaria scrapyard mod
text: Machinaria Machinaria adds a rusty scrapyard fragment and crafting gadgets. It also ships an optional Aetherhaven integration —you do not need Machinaria for Aetherhaven, and you do not need Aetherhaven for Machinaria’s core loop. What you get with both mods - Rivet Cogsworth , a robot mechanic freed from rust with black oil - Inn unlock after the rescue, then shop and house quests - A mechanics shop selling metal and gear from the Rusted Expanse (vanilla metal sets plus Machinaria blocks) - Quest board fetch jobs and a journal guide page for Rivet How to unlock Rivet 1. Install Machinaria and Aetherhaven on the same world or server. 2. In the Rusted Expanse, find a rusty robot, break it for the block, and throw it into oil. 3. Talk with Rivet when they wake, then meet them at the inn. 4. Accept shop and house quests from Rivet at the inn, and build the mechanics shop / house as usual. Full quest steps, schedule, and gift tastes: . Related Aetherhaven systems Shop spots and NPC restock work the same as for Vex and other workers—see . Plot tokens and blueprints use the same tools as the rest of town—see .

name: Crossmod integration
description: How other mods add villagers, buildings, dialogue, and more via asset packs
text: Crossmod integration with Aetherhaven This guide explains how another mod can add villagers, buildings, dialogue, quests, quest board pools, shop stock, prices, and field-rescue talk using assets (and a little Java when you need custom UI or conditions). Aetherhaven scans every registered asset pack for files under Server/Aetherhaven/ . Your mod should ship an asset pack ( IncludesAssetPack: true ) and list Aetherhaven as an optional or hard dependency so it loads in a sensible order. Manifest Use a hard Dependencies entry if your mod cannot run without Aetherhaven. Folder map Place content under your pack root: Path Purpose ------------------------------------------ ------------------------------------------------------------------- Server/Aetherhaven/Villagers/ Villager gameplay defs (dialogue trees, gifts, schedules, inn pool) Server/Aetherhaven/VillagerGiftPatches/ Append gift loves/likes/dislikes onto an existing villager Server/Aetherhaven/VillagerSchedules/ Weekly schedules by NPC role id Server/Aetherhaven/ScheduleLocations/ Custom schedule location symbols mapped to buildings Server/Aetherhaven/VillagerSchedulePatches/ Add, replace, or remove schedule times on existing roles Server/Aetherhaven/GuideTopics/ Journal guide markdown pages ( <locale /<topicId .md ) Server/Aetherhaven/GuidePatches/ Append guide hub sub-topics (e.g. under villagers ) Server/Aetherhaven/NpcRoles/ Engine NPC roles (only loaded when Aetherhaven is present) Server/Aetherhaven/NpcModels/ Optional NPC models for those roles (AH-gated) Server/Aetherhaven/Dialogue/ Full dialogue trees (same id overrides earlier packs) Server/Aetherhaven/DialoguePatches/ Inject choices/nodes into an existing tree Server/Aetherhaven/Quests/ Story / housing quests Server/Aetherhaven/QuestBoardExtensions/ Extra quest board fetch/hunt/raid entries Server/Aetherhaven/Buildings/ Construction definitions Server/Aetherhaven/ShopPrices/ Gold prices for shop spots Server/Aetherhaven/ShopLoot/ Shop spot loot tables (append or replace) Server/Aetherhaven/Townsfolk/ Townsfolk character pool Server/Aetherhaven/Personalities/ Personality traits Server/Prefabs/ Building prefabs referenced by constructions Server/Languages/en-US/ English lang keys Same content id from a later pack replaces an earlier pack for whole-file catalogs (villagers, dialogue trees, quests, buildings). Prices, loot, quest board pools, dialogue patches, gift patches, and schedule patches merge as described below. Villagers and NPC roles Crossmod villagers should put engine NPC roles under Server/Aetherhaven/NpcRoles/ , not under Server/NPC/Roles/ . Hytale only auto-loads Server/NPC/Roles/ ; Aetherhaven scans NpcRoles after its dialogue action, attitude groups, and Aetherhaven Human exist. If Aetherhaven is missing, those role files are ignored. 1. Add role JSON under Server/Aetherhaven/NpcRoles/ (role id = filename without .json ). Interact should open Aetherhaven dialogue ( OpenAetherhavenDialogue ), same pattern as Aetherhaven’s own roles. Optional component files can live under NpcRoles/.../Components/ (loaded before spawnable roles). 2. Optional appearance models under Server/Aetherhaven/NpcModels/ (model id = filename). You may still parent models to Aetherhaven Human or reuse Aetherhaven villager models that already ship with Aetherhaven under Server/Models/ . 3. Add a villager definition under Server/Aetherhaven/Villagers/ with matching npcRoleId , residentTreeId / visitorTreeId , gifts, schedule bindings, and so on. 4. For a shop worker who starts in the inn pool: set innPoolEligible , visitorBindingKind (e.g. visitor angler ), workConstructionId to your shop building id, and dialogueVillagerKind (resident kind after promotion, e.g. angler ). When that shop plot completes, Aetherhaven promotes the matching inn visitor if the shop quest is active or completed. Completing the quest alone does not move them; finishing the shop plot does. The shop quest should use grantPlotTokenConstructionId or grantPlotBl

Start with for the full folder map, villagers, buildings, dialogue patches, quests, and a worked example. Players looking for optional companion mods should see instead.

name: FAQ
description: Common questions about Aetherhaven and this journal
text: Frequently asked questions Answers here are meant as a quick reference while you play. If something still feels unclear, check Mechanics or Villagers for deeper detail. Will the mod have this feature? The answer is likely yes, but check the roadmap. Suggestions are always appreciated in the mod's discord. Where do I report bugs or suggest features? Bugs and feature requests can be submitted on the mods discord channel. Including your game version and whether you are single-player or on a server saves a lot of back-and-forth. Will saves break when the mod updates? We try to keep data migrations safe, but back up your world before major updates—especially on long-lived servers. Can I design my own buildings instead of using the existing prefabs? Integrated building tools are a planned feature for the mod. There's a good amount of configuration that needs to go into adding buildings at the moment. You can destroy/replace a building after its constructed but note that breaking/moving certain furniture/benches may prevent it from being used by villagers to fill their needs. For example moving their bed will result in them not being able to find it. There is a build submissions channel on the discord if you'd like your build to be featured in the main mod with credit.

name: Getting Started
description: Found a town and learn the first steps
text: Getting Started This page is a short path from an empty spot in the world to a town that earns gold and welcomes villagers. Start your town 1. Craft a town planning desk at a workbench. 2. Use the desk to craft a town charter and a plot placement staff . 3. Place the charter where you want the heart of the town to be. Your town gets a random name at first. Open the charter later to rename it. 4. Lyren the Elder appears. Talk to him to begin. The charter marks your town borders. You can read more about moving or replacing it on the Town charter page under Mechanics. Your first quest: build the inn Lyren asks you to raise the inn . In practice that means: 1. Talk to Lyren and accept the quest. He gives you the inn plot token (plot tokens for building quests come from the quest giver, not the planning desk). 2. Equip the plot placement staff and stake the inn footprint where it fits. 3. Bring the listed wood and stone to the plot sign and finish construction. When the inn is done, an innkeeper moves in. The inn is your first real building and a home base for town records. How the inn helps The inn is more than walls and a roof. Visitors can stay for a while. The inn holds up to two guests at a time. The guest list refreshes each morning unless you are working on a visitor quest that locks someone in place. The inn includes a town records shelf where you can check villager needs, invite friends to your town, and review gift history later on. Read Inn pool and visitors under Mechanics if you want the full picture on guests. Money and taxes Your town earns gold coins from a morning tithe . Each villager who counts as a resident pays based on how comfortable they are. Comfortable means their hunger , energy , and fun meters are in good shape. Tax collection runs while at least one member of your town is online. Open the treasury after you build a town hall to see coins add up and read a breakdown of who paid what. See Treasury and taxes under Mechanics for feast bonuses, policies, and other ways to earn more. Town hall and treasury After the inn is finished, talk to Lyren again. He offers raise the town hall . Build it the same way you built the inn: take the plot token from the quest, use the placement staff, then bring materials to the sign. The town hall holds the treasury block where your gold is stored. It also has another town records shelf and planning space. You need the hall if you want to deposit, withdraw, and study tax lines in one place. Who counts as a citizen Villagers become part of your town in two different ways. Workplace (required for a job in town) Build and finish the plot for their job (farm, shop, mill, and so on). Use the management block on that building to assign the villager to the workplace. Until they have a workplace, they are a guest or visitor, not a full resident tied to that job. House (optional) A house plot is not required for them to work. If you build a house and register them on it, they can sleep there at night. Sleep refills energy , which also helps the gold they pay each morning. For fun , build a park (see below). When you are ready to grow, take quest offers from villagers and visitors at the inn. Each new workplace you finish can add another resident. Tips Build a park if villagers often run low on fun . Park benches are the main way to refill fun. Open Mechanics and read the Villager needs page for hunger, energy, and fun in detail. Talk to villagers often and bring gifts if you want better prices, recipes, and milestone rewards. See Reputation under Mechanics. After the town hall , read Mechanics for the guild hall and guards , quest board , tourist portal , and other mid-game systems. Server hosts can use creative mode tools such as /ah starterkit to skip crafting. That is for testing, not the normal player path.

name: Mechanics
description: Tools, buildings, and town systems
text: Mechanics These pages describe how each major feature feels in play. Open the page you care about from the list on the left.

name: Building staff
description: Finish construction block by block
text: Building staff After a plot sign exists, the building staff lets you grow the structure in stages. Aim at highlighted blocks and confirm each batch. After pressing BUILD on a a plot sign, the building will start to build itself slowly. Using a Building Staff lets you speed up this process. While holding the staff green cubes will appear where blocks need to be placed. Holding secondary action (Right mouse button) with the staff while looking at these cubes will cause the cubes to expand and place the blocks for the building. If you can't find any green cubes you can use the primary action (Left mouse button) to shoot a projectile that homes in on the closest green cube. There are multiple tiers of building staff with increasing radius of building with the staff. Each staff grants extra max mana while you hold it. Placing blocks with secondary costs 1 mana per block from your mana bar. If you stop using secondary for a couple of seconds, mana refills faster while you still hold the staff. Tips Use scaffolding to reach higher places with the staff. Very large buildings are split into sections when building for performance.

name: Town charter
description: Found and grow your town
text: Town charter The charter is your town anchor. Place it once to create the town, name the place, and spawn the villager Elder to start your town building adventure. Tips If you dissolve the town, all villagers and buildings will be removed. You can move the charter using the button in its menu.

name: Commands
description: Chat commands for towns and server tools
text: Commands /aetherhaven and /ah are the same. Most players only need the For players section below. Access tells you which game mode gets the command by default. Permission is what server owners grant manually if access is not enough. Angle brackets are required; square brackets are optional. For players Town members - /ah town invite <player [townName] — Invite someone online to your town. - <player — Player username (must be online). - [townName] — Full town name with spaces. Omit for your town. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.invite - Access: Adventure - /ah town accept [townName] — Join a town that invited you. - [townName] — Full town name when you have more than one pending invite. Omit if you only have one. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.accept - Access: Adventure - /ah town decline [townName] — Turn down a town invite. - [townName] — Full town name when you have more than one pending invite. Omit if you only have one. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.decline - Access: Adventure - /ah town kick <player [townName] — Remove a member from your town. - <player — Member username (must be online). - [townName] — Full town name with spaces. Omit for your own town. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.kick - Access: Adventure - /ah town role <player <role [townName] — Set a member role: BUILD, QUEST, or BOTH. - <player — Member username (must be online). - <role — BUILD , QUEST , or BOTH . - [townName] — Full town name with spaces. Omit for your own town. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.role - Access: Adventure - /ah town leave — Leave a town you belong to (not as the founder). - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.leave - Access: Adventure Floating gifts - /ah floatinggift next — See when your next floating gift balloon can appear. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.floatinggift.next - Access: Adventure Path tool - /ah path revert <id — Undo a cemented path using the id from chat when you placed it. You also need path tool access in play. - <id — Path revert id (UUID) printed in chat when the path was placed. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.path.revert - Access: Adventure For world hosts These are for creative mode or people running the server. Not needed for normal town play. - /ah difficulty — Open the world difficulty menu for building costs. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.difficulty - Access: Creative - /ah reload — Reload mod config and data files from disk. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.reload - Access: Creative - /ah starterkit — Give yourself the starter tools (placement staff, charter, planning desk, building staff). - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.starterkit - Access: Creative - /ah exportskin [path] — Save your avatar skin as a model file. - [path] — Optional output path. Default is plugin data avatar exports with a timestamped filename. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.exportskin - Access: Creative - /ah exportskin <player [path] — Save another player's avatar skin (needs .other permission). - <player — Target player in the world. - [path] — Optional output path (same as above). - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.exportskin.other - Access: Creative - /ah time <hour — Set the in game schedule clock (villager routines use this clock). - <hour — Hour 0 to 23 (example 14 for 2 PM). - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.time - Access: Creative - /ah time dawn — Set that clock to 6:00 in the morning. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.time.dawn - Access: Creative - /ah plots finishassembly — Instantly finish every building still assembling in your town. - Optional --town or --player — Another town (staff; see Debug town targeting above). - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.pl

name: Floating gifts
description: Sky presents for active towns
text: Floating gifts Sometimes a wrapped gift drifts above town. Shoot it down before it floats away. Gifts come in three colors. Each color holds different treasures inside a matching gift box. White gifts often hold building blueprints, gold coins, and useful supplies. Green gifts hold jewelry, gold coins, and useful supplies. Red gifts hold furniture pieces, gold coins, and useful supplies.

name: Geodes
description: Crack rocks for gems
text: Geodes Geodes are chunky rocks found rarely when mining ores and crystals. The town's blacksmith can crack them open for you at a price. Ores, crystal shards, and rarely gems can be obtained by cracking open geodes. If the blacksmith likes you enough he will share a recipe for the Geode Anvil that will open geodes for free.

name: Guild hall and guards
description: Adventurers, hired guards, patrol routes, and command mode
text: Guild hall and guards The guild hall is a mid-game civic building where adventurers gather. Lyra Fairhollow asks you to raise it after the town hall is standing. See her villager page for the build quest. Once the hall is finished you can hire guards , draw patrol routes , and use the command post for a top-down battlefield view. Hiring guards Talk to adventurers at the guild hall to hire them as guards . Guards come as knights, archers, and mages. They patrol your town and fight hostile mobs. They will not attack villagers, tourists, or other guards. Guards need a route or orders to know where to go. Unassigned guards still defend nearby threats when they can. Patrol wand Craft the patrol wand at the town planning desk . Blue sparkles mark saved routes only while you hold the wand. Build mode (default) Right click the ground — add a patrol point. Right click a point — remove it. Left click a point on a saved route — select that route for editing. F — name and save the route (needs at least two points). R — toggle closed loop (guards loop from last point back to first) vs back and forth . E — start a fresh route. Q — switch to Assign mode. Assign mode Left click a route point — select a saved route. F — open the guard list and assign someone to the route. E — clear the guard from the selected route. Q — switch to Build mode. Selected routes glow green ; other routes stay blue . Guards with more than one route take turns walking each loop. Command post Place a guard command post stool in town (creative or progression unlock). Use it to enter command mode — a top-down RTS-style view of your town. Camera and selection WASD — pan the battlefield view. Space / Ctrl — fly up and down to zoom. Scroll or number keys — switch command tools. Click a guard — select them. Shift + click — add or remove from selection. Drag a box — select many guards at once. Orders Attack-move / Move tool — right click the ground to send selected guards. Ability1 switches between attack-move and move-only. Ability2 stops selected guards. Focus fire tool — right click a creature to focus your guards on it. Stance tool — Ability1 cycles combat stance (defensive, aggressive, stand ground, hold fire) for selected guards. Free tool — right click to release selected guards from your orders. Select all / by type — roster buttons on the HUD. Leave command tool (hotbar slot 8) — exit command mode. The command post must sit inside your town lands to work. You need at least one hired guard. Quest board The guild hall also holds the quest board for daily fetch, hunt, and raid jobs. See Quest board under Mechanics.

name: Inn pool and visitors
description: Rotating guests at the inn
text: Inn pool and visitors The inn can host visitors who are not full time residents. The inn can hold up to 2 visitors at a time, refreshing and rerolling daily at dawn. If you have accepted a visitors quest they are locked in and won't be rerolled. Debugging If the inn's visitors don't seem to be showing up or are messed up in some way, try running the /ah villager fixinn command.

name: Jewelry
description: Rings, necklaces, and stats
text: Jewelry Jewelry can be occassionally found in loot chests around the world. Newly found jewelry is unidentified. Bring it to the Vex the Merchant to identify the effects of the jewelry. Jewelry comes in 5 rarities (Common, Uncommon, Rare, Mythic, and Legendary). Gold is stronger than silver and Necklaces are stronger than rings. The type of gemstones determines which stats the jewelry affects. If the merchant likes you enough he will share the recipes for the Appraisal Bench and the Jewlery Crafting Bench. The Appraisal Bench will appraise jewelry for free. The Jewelry Crafting Bench allows the player to craft their own jewelry using gold/silver ingots, gemstones, and life essence. The more life essence provided, the higher the quality. Gemstone stats Each gemstone type sets which three player stats the piece can roll. The exact numbers depend on rarity, metal, and ring vs necklace. Zephyr — Stamina, Signature Energy, Oxygen Topaz — Stamina, Signature Energy, Ammo Emerald — Health, Mana, Oxygen Diamond — Health, Stamina, Mana Sapphire — Mana, Stamina, Oxygen Ruby — Health, Stamina, Ammo Voidstone — Mana, Signature Energy, Ammo Tips Extra jewelry makes great gifts for villagers. See Reputation under Mechanics for how gifting affects friendship.

name: Path designer shovel
description: Lay out spline paths, styles, and removal
text: Path designer shovel The path designer shovel lets you draw curved paths through town, preview them, and place blocks on the ground. A status panel with key hints appears while you hold the tool. Craft it at the town planning desk . Modes Press Q to cycle through five modes: 1. Move — add and reposition control nodes to shape the path. 2. Rotate — turn the selected node to bend the spline. 3. Place — cement the finished path onto the ground. 4. Remove — view placed paths (highlighted in orange) and delete ones you no longer want. 5. Style designer — create and edit path styles in a chest grid. The HUD reminds you to switch to Place mode when you are ready to lay path blocks. Controls by mode Move, Rotate, and Place Secondary (right click) on ground — add a node. Secondary while aiming at a node — remove that node. Primary (left click) on a node — select it. Primary on ground (Move mode) — move the selected node. F (Rotate mode) — nudge the selected node's direction. F (Place mode) — place the path on the ground. E — cycle path width. R — cycle path style. Q — next mode. Remove Primary — select a placed path. F — remove the selected path. Q — next mode. Style designer F — open the style manager (double-chest grid for weighted block columns). E — save the path style (while the chest is open). Q — next mode. Preview visuals While editing, white nodes and lines show the spline. A brown preview marks where blocks will go, with green edges at the sides. Remove mode shows committed paths in orange instead. Tips Shape the spline in Move and Rotate first, then switch to Place and press F to cement it. Build custom looks in Style designer — each style is a weighted column of blocks rolled along the path width. Paths persist in the world and in your town save.

name: Player shop and shop spots
description: NPC stalls, your own shop, and buying in the world
text: Player shop and shop spots Shop spot blocks live inside finished building plots. They let NPCs and players sell items in the world instead of only through dialogue menus. NPC shops Villager shops — Vex's general store , the Florist, Pyrotechnic, Crystal Keeper, and others — restock at dawn from loot tables. Each spot shows a floating item display; the stall's facing rotates the display. F (use) — open the buy panel with quantity controls (±1, ±10, max). Look-at HUD — shows item name, price, and stock while you aim at a stocked spot. Vex now runs a general store selling furniture, blocks, and consumables through shop spots in his market stall and related buildings. Your own shop After Vex's market stall is built, Vex offers Your Own Shop : 1. Take the player shop plot token from Vex. 2. Stake and build the player shop prefab. 3. Find Vex and close the quest in dialogue. The player shop includes shop spot blocks and a shop safe that holds gold from your sales. Listing items Right click a shop spot while holding an item — list it for sale (player-controlled spots only). Right click again on your own listing — remove it from the spot. Buyers press F on stocked spots to purchase. You receive a notification when someone buys your listing, and gold collects in the shop safe . Who shops Villagers and tourists browse player shop spots and buy listed items when they visit town. Price and stock matter — empty spots are skipped. Permissions Town members need permission to sell on player shop spots. The town owner can adjust member permissions from the town records shelf. See Plot tokens under Mechanics for crafting plot tokens at the plot crafting bench.

name: Plot creator staff
description: Turn a build into a custom town building definition
text: Plot creator staff The plot creator staff registers custom buildings you built in the world: footprint, specialty blocks, prefab export, costs, and (optionally) a live plot in your town. Most players should use Decoration or Variant , not the full workplace types below. Open your town journal → Guide → Mechanics → Plot creator staff (this page) while learning the flow. In play: equip the staff, press F to start or open the current step panel, primary-click blocks in the world, Q / E previous / next step, R to cancel. Recommended paths Goal Building type Notes ------ ---------------- ------- Cosmetic build, no jobs Decoration Optional town records shelf; no production or villager logic. Alternate look for an existing building Variant Pick which main building it counts as (house, barn, inn, etc.). Substeps follow that main type. New workplace / production plot (modding) Work For adding new workplace types; needs management block, production storage, and a work surface POI. Building types (picker) Decoration — Parks, props, and builds that should not act as homes, shops, or workplaces. Minimal required spots. Variant — A prefab that counts as another building id already in the mod (for example a custom house that counts as plot house ). You choose the main type from the dropdown; important spots match that main building. Home — Residential plot: town records shelf + sleep POI. Work — Developer / content author use. Defines a new workplace -style plot: town records shelf, production storage, and a work-surface POI. Use when you are adding a new production or job building type, not for normal cosmetic variants. Amenity — Fun or leisure (park, altar-style amenity): shelf + fun/sit POI. Shop — Stall or shop counter: shelf + shop-tagged work POI. Inn — Full inn layout: shelf, work surface, beds, eat spot, innkeeper and visitor spawns (and optional guild master spawn slot). Town hall — Civic hub: shelf, treasury block, planning desk POI. Guild hall — Adventurer guild: shelf, work surface, adventurer spawn points. Overlap and confusion - Variant vs Home / Work / … — Variant is for “looks different, behaves like X.” Pick Variant + main type, not Home , if you are reskinning an existing gameplay building. - Work vs Shop — Shop is for merchant stalls. Work is for farms, mills, forges, and other production workplaces. - Amenity vs Decoration — Decoration has almost no gameplay hooks. Amenity sets fun/amenity tags and POIs for villager schedules. - Inn , Town hall , and Guild hall are full templates; use Variant only if you are matching one of those templates on purpose. Flow (short) 1. Mark two opposite corners and an outside plot-sign corner. 2. Choose building type (and variant of if applicable). 3. Place important spots (blocks are given one at a time per substep). 4. Enter name and id (prefab filename follows the id). 5. Edit tags if needed. 6. Open building settings (F): treasury gold cost, self-build days, empty-space prefab option, and assembly sections. 7. Export prefab with F on the save-shape step (uses settings from step 6). 8. Set build materials (virtual chest; items return to you when you continue). 9. Review and save. Permissions By default, config may allow everyone to use the plot creator; servers can require the aetherhaven.plot.creator permission instead.

name: Plot placement staff
description: Claim land and stamp building footprints
text: Plot placement staff This staff is how you pick where a new plot lives. Equip it, choose a construction, then place the sign on solid ground.

name: Plot tokens
description: Items that unlock special builds
text: Plot tokens Plot tokens are items you hold in inventory to pick a building type on the plot placement staff , then stake the footprint in the world. Plot crafting bench Craft plot tokens at the plot crafting bench . The bench shows a 3D preview of the building before you commit materials. Craft the bench at the town planning desk , then place it like any workstation. Most story quests still hand you the first token directly from the quest giver. After that, replacements and extra copies usually come from the bench. Plot blueprints Some buildings are gated behind plot blueprints instead of dropping ready-made tokens from balloons. 1. Use the blueprint item to permanently unlock that plot at your plot crafting bench. 2. Open the bench and craft the plot token (materials plus gold, same as other tokens). 3. Equip the plot placement staff and stake the footprint. White floating gifts often carry blueprints. Green gifts favor jewelry; red gifts favor furniture. Balloon gifts are rarer than before. Salvage Extra plot tokens — including variant tokens from gifts — can be salvaged for gold coins at a workbench when you do not need another copy. Tips Read Player shop and shop spots under Mechanics if a building includes merchant stalls. Florist, Pyrotechnic, and Crystal Keeper shop quests grant blueprints rather than direct tokens.

name: Production wardrobe
description: Outfits and output for production buildings
text: Production wardrobe Production buildings use a wardrobe style chest for configuring and accessing the generated resources. Find the wardrobe in the building and interact with it to open the production window. You can cycle through the available resources to produce using the arrows. Each resource type is stored seperately. Choosing multiple of the same resource increases the speed at which it is produced. The unlocks page lets you unlock new resources to generate at the cost of some of that resource and gold coins. In the future you will be able to upgrade the max storage and production speed of buildings.

name: Purification powder
description: Cleanse cursed jewelry rolls
text: Purification powder Purification powder allows the player to remove enemy spawn points in generated structures. While holding the powder the player will be able to see small spinning versions of mobs where they would periodically spawn in the structure. Using the powder on this will remove the spawn point permanently. Unlocked by befriending the Priestess.

name: Quest board
description: Daily fetch, hunt, and raid jobs at the guild hall
text: Quest board The quest board in the guild hall posts daily work for your town. Interact with the board to open a three-card panel showing today's jobs. New cards refresh each dawn when at least one member of your town is online. Job types Fetch A townsfolk needs supplies brought to town. Accept the job, gather the listed items, and turn them in through that villager's dialogue . Rank tiers gate harder requests and better rewards. Hunt Kill a certain number of a mob type, then report back to the quest giver. Progress shows on the card and in your journal. Raid A group of hostiles spawns on the outskirts of town and marches toward your borders. Kill every mob in the group to complete the contract. Map markers and a raid health bar show which enemies count toward the quest. Rank and rewards Each completed board quest grants rank XP for your town. Higher town rank unlocks tougher tiers with better payouts. Cards show a time limit in days — finish before it expires or the slot clears at dawn. Rewards include gold, items, and reputation with the posting villager when the quest grants it. Tracking Active board quests appear on the Quests tab of your town journal alongside story quests. You can abandon a board quest from the journal if you change your mind. See Guild hall and guards under Mechanics for how to build the hall where the board lives.

name: Reputation
description: Friendship, gifts, and milestone rewards
text: Reputation Reputation is how much a villager trusts and likes you. It is personal: your score with the farmer does not change your score with the merchant. The meter runs from 0 to 100. Higher reputation unlocks milestone rewards and sometimes new recipes. Milestone progress and gift taste spoilers for each character are in the Villagers tab of your town journal. Gift history is on the town records shelf in the inn or town hall. Ways to raise reputation Talk each day The first time you speak with a villager after a new morning, you earn a small reputation bonus. Stop by while you are already walking the town. It adds up over time. Give gifts During dialogue, choose the gift option while holding an item in your hand. The villager reacts based on whether they love, like, feel neutral about, or dislike the gift. Better reactions give more reputation. A gift they dislike can lower it. You can only give so many gifts per villager per week, so save strong gifts for people you are trying to impress. Complete quests Story quests from the Elder, innkeeper, and other residents often grant reputation when you finish them. The Quests tab in your journal shows item rewards and reputation lines when a quest grants them. Milestone rewards Each villager has their own friendship milestones at set reputation levels (not every character uses the same steps). When you cross a threshold, a reward waits for you. Talk to that villager to receive it. Rewards can be items, recipe knowledge, or a special thank-you conversation. If you pass several milestones at once, talk once and work through what they owe you. The Villagers tab in your journal lists each character and their milestones without spoiling every gift preference. Gift history on the town records shelf Open the town records shelf (inn or town hall) and browse by villager. You can see gifts you already gave and how they felt about each one. That helps you avoid repeating mistakes and plan the next present. Tips Rings and necklaces are on every town villager's liked gifts list. Jewelry is a reliable choice before you learn someone's personal favorites. Unidentified jewelry still counts once it is a real ring or necklace in your hand. Read Jewelry under Mechanics for finding and crafting pieces. Combine daily visits, quest lines, and thoughtful gifts on the villagers you care about most. Milestone rewards are claimed in person. If you crossed a threshold and nothing happened, find them in the world and start dialogue.

name: Sprinklers
description: Water many farm cells at once
text: Sprinklers Sprinklers are metal friends for big fields. Activate one and it refreshes crops in an area aroudn the sprinkler once daily at dawn. It can also be activated manually by using the block. Unlocked by befriending the Farmer. There are four tiers of sprinkler to unlock with increasing radius of watering.

name: Tourist portal
description: Daily visitors who shop and can move in
text: Tourist portal The tourist portal draws travelers from beyond your town borders. Lyren the Elder offers the build quest after the town hall is standing. Building the portal 1. Talk to Lyren and accept the tourist portal quest. 2. Take the tourist portal plot token from Lyren. 3. Stake and build the tourist portal prefab. 4. Find Lyren and close the quest in dialogue. Daily visits Each morning, tourists can arrive through the portal. They walk around town, browse shop spots (including your player shop), and leave at night . Tourists are hand-picked characters with personality traits that shape their dialogue. They are separate from inn visitors — see Inn pool and visitors under Mechanics for the inn's two-guest rotation. Inviting tourists to stay If you want a tourist to become a permanent resident, offer them a house : 1. Build a house plot and assign them on the management block through the appropriate housing quest flow. 2. Once registered, they count toward town life like other residents. Tourists who shop at player listings spend real gold from their pockets — a good reason to stock your shop spots with useful goods. Tips Finish Your Own Shop (from Vex) before expecting much tourist spending — they buy from player shop spots. The portal and inn serve different roles: the inn locks story visitors for quests; the portal brings repeat tourists each day.

name: Town records shelf
description: Browse town info in the world
text: Town records shelf The town records shelf is a hub of information and controls for your town. In the needs tab you can view the current needs of all the villagers as well as teleport them to you using the teleport button. You can also check villagers gift preferences. It will show any gifts you've given to each villager and their response to it. In the town management tab you can invite and manage players in your town. You can click on a player name to manage their town permissions. You can use the move button to rearrange your building. (Be careful moving buildings, anything that wasn't part of the building when it was placed will be destoyed, including entities like animals). Production building upgrades Open the shelf on a production building (farm, lumber mill, miner's hut, barn, and similar workplaces) to upgrade it. Upgrades improve output or capacity depending on the building type. Costs and tiers are shown in the shelf UI — pay from town resources or materials as listed. Upgrades persist with the plot. Check the shelf after finishing a new workplace to see what the first tier unlocks.

name: Treasury and taxes
description: Gold flow for the town
text: Treasury and taxes The treasury block holds town gold. Residents pay a morning tithe based on their current need fulfillment. The town will generate taxes as long as one town member is on the server, even in unloaded chunks. It will not generate while no town members are online. A breakdown of taxes can be viewed in the second tab. There are several additional ways to increase how much you make from taxes, such as feasts, the founder statue, and town policies.

name: Villager needs
description: Hunger, energy, fun, and where villagers go
text: Villager needs Every villager in town tracks three needs: hunger , energy , and fun . Each meter runs from empty to full. You can see them on the town records shelf in the inn or town hall, under the Needs tab. Why needs matter Villagers slowly get hungrier, tire out, and want entertainment as the day goes on. When a meter is low, they look for the right place in town to fix it. Needs also tie into taxes . Each morning, residents pay gold into the treasury. The amount depends partly on how comfortable they are. Comfortable villagers pay more. Keeping meters up is good for them and for your town wallet. Points of interest Finished buildings add spots villagers can use: beds, benches, counters, workbenches, and similar blocks. Think of each spot as a small action in the world. Beds refill energy only (including beds in houses at night). Benches and seats with a fun spot refill fun only, including park benches. Meal spots (inn hearth, restaurant chairs, counters, and food storage) refill hunger only. Workbenches and shop counters are for the job. They do not refill any need by themselves. Different plots place different spots. A farm has farming benches. An inn has beds and meal space. A park has outdoor benches meant for relaxing. How villagers pick a spot Villagers follow a daily schedule, but a very low meter can pull them away for a while. If hunger is critical, they head for food. If energy is low, they seek a bed. If fun is low, they look for a bench or social spot. You do not need to click each spot yourself. Build the right plots and they will find them as the day runs. Houses at night A house is optional. Villagers only need their workplace plot to hold a job in town. If you assign someone to a house, they can sleep there at night. That sleep refills energy , which keeps them comfortable for the next morning tithe. Use a park when fun is the problem. Tips If fun is always the lowest meter, stake a park plot from your planning desk. Park benches are built for relaxing. Use the records shelf Needs tab to see everyone at a glance and teleport a villager to you if you want to check on them. Feasts and some town policies can change how much gold you earn from comfortable residents. Read Treasury and taxes for the money side.

text: Vex Sunderlane runs a general store through shop spots in the market stall once it is built. Stock restocks at dawn; press F on a spot to buy. See Player shop and shop spots under Mechanics. Quests Vex's home Vex can stack inventory anywhere. They still want a dry corner that answers to their knock. 1. Take the house plot token from Vex. 2. Stake and build the house prefab. 3. Assign Vex as resident on the house management block. 4. Find Vex and close the quest in dialogue. Vex's market stall Give Vex a counter and a roof so salvage has somewhere honest to land. 1. Take the market stall plot token from Vex. 2. Stake and build the market stall prefab. 3. Find Vex at the stall and close the quest in dialogue. Your own shop Build a shop where you can sell goods to townsfolk and tourists. 1. Finish Vex's market stall first. 2. Take the player shop plot token from Vex. 3. Stake and build the player shop prefab. 4. Find Vex and close the quest in dialogue. name: Grubble Sparkmatch
description: Quests, friendship, schedule, and gifts for Grubble Sparkmatch.
text: Grubble Sparkmatch is a goblin pyrotechnic who sells explosives. You must find and free him in the world before he will visit the inn. After the rescue, he can open a bomb shop in town. Use Show weekly schedule below to see where Grubble goes each day. Quests Grubble's big escape While exploring, you may find Grubble trapped in a spider cocoon. Free him to complete this quest. He will then start appearing at the inn. Grubble's bomb shop Grubble wants a proper shop where he can sell his boom things to the town. 1. Talk to Grubble at the inn and accept the quest. 2. Take the shop blueprint from Grubble. 3. Use the blueprint at your plot crafting bench to learn the bomb shop. 4. Craft a shop plot token and build the bomb shop prefab. 5. Find Grubble at the shop and close the quest in dialogue. Grubble's home Even a goblin who loves loud noises needs a quiet bed sometimes. 1. Take the house plot token from Grubble. 2. Stake and build the house prefab. 3. Assign Grubble as resident on the house management block. 4. Find Grubble and close the quest in dialogue.

name: Welcome
description: Start here to learn Aetherhaven in your journal
text: Welcome to the guide This book lives inside your town journal. Pick a topic on the left to read more. Getting Started walks you through founding a town, your first buildings, and how money flows in. Mechanics explains tools, buildings, and systems you will use around town. Villagers introduces each resident, their story quests, reputation gifts, and weekly routines. Gift taste spoilers stay hidden until you choose to show them.
